provider: Quark TV and UC TV (夸克网盘 TV版, UC网盘 TV版)
category: TV-edition OAuth client for a Chinese pan

free_tier.stated: Quark free 300 GB plus one-off 1 TB gift campaigns; two documented campaigns give 2 TB total. UC's free base is 10 GB

per_object_cap.stated: Not published for the TV client

retention.stated: The gift campaigns are one-off per account and campaign-gated. No retention clock on stored files

egress.terms: Quark free is shaped to about 1.7 MB/s and about 5 MB/s at peak for 88VIP. The TV client streams in original quality without downloading, which is why the community uses it

tooling: a reverse-engineered TV OAuth client, fully documented in source: the OpenList quark_uc_tv driver hard-codes api https://open-api-drive.quark.cn for Quark and https://open-api-drive.uc.cn for UC, with a public client id, a TV sign key, an app version and a channel. WebDAV comes out once mounted
chaining: The TV OAuth reads an account through a clean API with no client, so it is a serving and STRM path and not a write path. Paired with a writable pan it covers both directions, which is why the community keeps it alive

limits.value: the TV client is read-only by design: the driver sets NoUpload and NoOverwriteUpload
free egress shaped to about 1.7 MB/s

identity_cost.detail: a Quark or UC account, which is phone-bound in practice; the TV client's own login path exists but does not remove the account requirement

reliability_note: The TV client's client id and sign key are public constants that Alibaba rotates, and when they rotate every mount breaks until the driver is re-patched. The free-tier space campaigns are monthly and quantity-capped, so they are a lottery and not a capacity plan

binding_note: 300 GB free, and the TV client cannot write at all, so the direction that fails is the write side: it is a download-and-stream path with no upload, which makes it a serving helper and not a store.
notes: The canonical inverse of the public-instance problem. There an instance advertises a write it refuses; here a client is documented as read-only by design. Both are cases where the API's write surface must be read from the driver's own flags and not from the marketing page.
